keywords.meaning: after making the effort; since you've gone to the trouble; specially
keywords.nuance: せっかく emphasizes that someone invested effort, time, money, or a valuable opportunity. It often means that the opportunity should not be wasted, or that it is a shame the effort was not rewarded. Unlike やっと, which focuses on relief after difficulty, せっかく focuses on the value of the effort itself.
keywords.example: せっかく日本に来たんだから、寿司を食べよう。
keywords.exampleTranslation: Since we've come all the way to Japan, let's eat sushi.

commonPitfall.title: Common Pitfall
commonPitfall.body: Don't translate せっかく as simply 'especially.' Think 'after all that effort' or 'since we already went to the trouble.' English often does not translate it directly.

questions.prompt: せっかく作ったのに、誰も食べなかった。
questions.hint: The speaker is disappointed because effort was wasted.
questions.answer: Even though I went to the trouble of making it, nobody ate it.

questions.prompt: せっかくの休みだから、ゆっくりしよう。
questions.hint: A valuable opportunity shouldn't be wasted.
questions.answer: Since we have this precious day off, let's take it easy.

questions.prompt: せっかく日本語を勉強しているんだから、日本人と話してみたら？
questions.hint: The speaker encourages someone to make use of their effort.
questions.answer: Since you're already studying Japanese, why don't you try speaking with Japanese people?

questions.prompt: せっかく買ったのに、一度も使っていない。
questions.hint: Something was purchased but never used.
questions.answer: Even though I went to the trouble of buying it, I haven't used it even once.

productionQuestions.prompt: Since we're already here, let's take some pictures.
productionQuestions.hint: Use 〜んだから to naturally express 'since we've already come all this way.'

referenceAnswers.answer: せっかく来たんだから、写真を撮ろう。
referenceAnswers.note: Uses 〜んだから to naturally express 'since we've already come all this way.'

referenceAnswers.answer: せっかくここまで来たし、写真を撮ろう。
referenceAnswers.note: Adds ここまで ('all the way here'), making the effort more explicit.

productionQuestions.prompt: I studied so much, but I forgot everything.
productionQuestions.hint: Use 〜のに to show that the effort was wasted.

referenceAnswers.answer: せっかく勉強したのに、全部忘れてしまった。
referenceAnswers.note: A classic use of せっかく showing disappointment that the effort was wasted.

referenceAnswers.answer: たくさん勉強したのに、結局忘れてしまった。
referenceAnswers.note: Doesn't use せっかく, but expresses a similar idea naturally.

productionQuestions.prompt: She bought a nice camera but never uses it.
productionQuestions.hint: Use 一度も with a negative form for 'never.'

referenceAnswers.answer: せっかくいいカメラを買ったのに、一度も使っていない。
いいカメラを買ったのに、全然使っていない。
referenceAnswers.note: More direct, but loses the nuance that the purchase itself was valuable.

productionQuestions.prompt: Since you're already studying Japanese, you should visit Japan someday.
productionQuestions.hint: Use 〜んだから to encourage someone to make good use of their effort.

referenceAnswers.answer: せっかく日本語を勉強しているんだから、いつか日本へ行ったほうがいいよ。
referenceAnswers.note: Encourages someone to make good use of their effort.

referenceAnswers.answer: 日本語を勉強しているなら、いつか日本へ行ってみたら？
referenceAnswers.note: Very natural, but it doesn't emphasize the value of the effort the way せっかく does.
